source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem where the set of arms is the unit sphere in $\Real^r$, and $W^{\BF u}_t$ has a standard normal distribution ... If $\BF Z$ has a multivariate normal distribution with mean $\BF 0$ and covariance matrix $\BF I_r / r$, then for all policies $\psi$ and every $T \geq r^2$, ${\rm Risk} ( T, \psi ) \geq 0.006 \,r\, \sqrt{T}$.

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consequently, for any policy $\psi$ and $T \geq r^2$, there exists $\BF z \in \Real^r$ such that ${\rm Regret} \left( \BF z, T, \psi \right) \geq 0.006 \, r \, \sqrt{T}$.

source.label: theorem:greedy-regret
source.quote: Suppose that Assumption 1 holds and that the sets $\CAL U_r$ satisfy the SBAR($J$) condition. Then, there exists a positive constant $a_1$ ... such that for any $\BF z \in \Real^r \setminus \{\BF 0\}$ and $T \geq r$, ${\rm Regret} ( \BF z, T, \textsc{PEGE} ) \leq a_1 ( \norm{\BF z} + \frac{1}{\norm{\BF z}} ) r \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: PEGE does not depend on T, so anytime. Unspecified constant a_1.

symbols.a_2: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, J, M

source.label: theorem:greedy-regret
source.quote: Then, there exists a positive constant $a_2$ that depends only on $\sigma_0$, $\bar{u}$, $\lambda_0$, $J$, and $M$, such that for any $T \geq r$, ${\rm Risk} ( T, \textsc{PEGE} ) \leq a_2 \, r \, \sqrt{T}$.

source.label: co:matching-upper-bounds
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem where the set of arms is the unit sphere in $\Real^r$, and where $W^{\BF u}_t$ has a standard normal distribution ... there exists an absolute constant $a_3$ such that for any $\BF z \in \Real^r \setminus \{\BF 0\}$ and $T \geq r$, ${\rm Regret} ( \BF z, T, \textsc{PEGE} ) \leq a_3 ( \norm{\BF z} + \frac{1}{\norm{\BF z}} ) r \sqrt{T}$.

source.label: co:matching-upper-bounds
source.quote: Moreover, if $\BF Z$ has a multivariate normal distribution with mean $\BF 0$ and covariance matrix $\BF I_r / r$, then for all $T \geq r$, ${\rm Risk} ( T, \textsc{PEGE} ) \leq a_3 \, r \sqrt{T}$.
